title: Correct dispatcher fairness regression causing short-request latency spikes
creator: Lin Chen
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers reported sudden p95/p99 latency spikes for short (<=128 token) requests across Hosted and Dedicated deployments over the last 10 days. The root cause is a regression in the continuous batching dispatcher that allowed long-context requests to dominate batch formation and prevented fast-path dispatch for low-token requests on mixed-load machines. This ticket tracks the investigation, bugfix, tests, and rollout for a fairness restoration and short-request fastpath.

Scope: Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, Private VPC runtime (config-dependent). Similar but separate configuration behaviors observed in Dedicated autoscaled pools where preemption was disabled for burst nodes.

Customer escalations:
- Customer A (fintech) — production errors and user-visible latency, on Hosted.
- Customer B (instore-search, Dedicated) — SLO violations during peak, manual failover.
- Customer C (private deployment) — reported high tail latency after upgrade to runtime-1.25.

Impact metrics observed (representative):
- Small request p95: previous baseline ~65ms -> incident peaks ~420ms.
- Queue depth increase for 'short' priority class: 3x baseline.
- KV-cache eviction churn correlated with long-request batching.

Why this is unique from earlier issues: earlier tickets focused on queue starvation broadly; this regression is introduced by a merge that changed bin-merge weighting and inadvertently disabled age-based preemption when bins contain mixed token-length requests. It also exposes a token-estimation bug in the client-side router that under-estimates long-context requests in some code paths, causing them to end up in small-request bins and amplify tail effects.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy runtime-1.25 with continuous-batcher config 'adaptive_mix=true' and preemption disabled on burst nodes.
2) Generate mixed load: 70% small requests (<=64 tokens) at 150rps + 30% long requests (>=4096 tokens) at 10rps targeted to same worker pool.
3) Observe batch formation and p95 for small requests climb above 300ms after 30s.
4) Add client-side long-request estimation bypass to see under-estimation reproduces bin misassignment.

Repro notes: Requires realistic KV-cache usage pattern to see eviction amplification. A synthetic test harness with mocked KV works but underestimates the magnitude seen in production.
investigation_log:
2025-02-14: Pager alert triggered for Customer A p95>300ms (Lin Chen triaged).
2025-02-14 02:10 UTC: Captured traces showing small-request futures blocked for duration of long-request kernel executions.
2025-02-15: Staging run with mixed traffic reproduces elevated short-request tail.
2025-02-16: Bisect identified merge MR #4920 changed bin-merge weighting (author: M. Torres).
2025-02-18: Reproduced token-estimation misbehavior in node router; found edge-case in tokenizer-length cache invalidation.
2025-02-20: Hotfix candidate implemented to restore age-priority in dispatcher and to add explicit small-request fastpath.
2025-02-21: Canary on Hosted (2 nodes) showed p95 improvement for small-requests from 420ms -> 120ms under test load.
2025-02-25: Dedicated customer B confirmed reduction in SLO violations on canary capacity.
2025-03-01: Private customer C reproduced locally and validated patch on their runtime build.
decisions:
- Revert the bin-merge weighting change that removed age-based decay.
- Implement dedicated 'short-request' fastpath that bypasses normal merging when request token estimate <= 128 and queue wait > 10ms.
- Add explicit preemption hook for Dedicated burst nodes and make it configurable per pool.
- Fix tokenizer-length cache invalidation to avoid under-estimating long requests in the router.
- Do NOT apply aggressive batching for mixed-load pools by default; expose 'adaptive_mix' as opt-in for customers with homogeneous workloads.
rollback_plan:
If post-deploy regressions appear:
- Re-enable previous dispatcher config (feature-flag revert) to restore pre-incident behavior.
- For Dedicated: scale additional nodes to drain backlog and temporarily pin affected customers to isolated pools.
- Notify affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1 (Hosted canary): apply patch to 3 canary nodes in us-west-2, run synthetic mixed-load for 2 hours, monitor p95/p99 and queue depths.
Stage 2 (Hosted bulk): ramp to 30% of capacity over 6 hours if metrics good.
Stage 3 (Dedicated): coordinate with account ops to apply to one customer-facing pool, verify SLOs for 24h.
Stage 4 (Private): publish patch and config guidance; offer assisted upgrade for customers who reported the issue.
Post-deploy: monitor for 72h and run a postmortem with customer success.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for bin-merge logic and age-decay behavior.
- Regression tests for token-length estimation and tokenizer-length cache invalidation.
- Synthetic mixed-load performance harness that reproduces short+long mixes at scale (run in CI and internal perf lab).
- Nightly canary job that runs this mixed-load and fails if short-request p95 > 150ms.
- Load test on Dedicated staging pool with real customer traces replayed (sanitized).
acceptance_criteria:
- Short-request p95 on mixed-load perf harness reduced to <=150ms under target RPS.
- No increase in long-request tail latency beyond 10% vs baseline.
- Customer A and B confirm SLO restoration in production.
- Observability: new dashboards for per-priority queue depth and per-pool preemption counters reporting.
- All unit and integration tests green in CI and canary for 72h.
